extracted.intended_audience: Policy makers within DoD and the Marine Corps; Regional Contracting Officers and installation-level acquisition personnel
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for applying OMB Circular A-76 to outsourcing (competitive sourcing) of installation support services in the Department of Defense, including process steps, exemptions, documentation requirements, risk management, and lessons learned. Focused on helping Regional Contracting Officers identify services suitable for competition and manage associated issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy: Government should not compete with private sector
rubrics_metrics.description: "In the process of governing, the Government should not compete with its citizens... it has been and continues to be the general policy of the Government to rely on commercial sources to supply products and services the Government needs."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the overarching A-76 policy rationale driving competitive sourcing efforts; use it to assess whether an activity is commercial and appropriate for competition rather than inherently governmental work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inherently governmental functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions "so intimately related to the public interest as to mandate performance by Governmental employees."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determination rests on factors including level of governmental control, ministerial nature of the function, and distinguishing recurring operations from oversight. Use OFPP guidance and Appendix C (functions listed by OFPP) to screen activities that are excluded from competitive sourcing.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAIR Act inventory requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Federal Activities Inventory Reform Act (FAIR Act) each agency head must submit a list of activities they consider not inherently governmental.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should maintain and use the FAIR Act inventory when identifying functions for A-76 studies; the Act does not mandate outsourcing but frames which activities are candidates for competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-comparison exemptions: National defense or intelligence security
rubrics_metrics.description: Category listed among situations where cost comparisons are not required: National Defense or Intelligence Security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an activity implicates national defense/intelligence security, a cost comparison under A-76 may be unnecessary; treat such activities as exempt from the A-76 cost-comparison process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-comparison exemptions: Patient care
rubrics_metrics.description: Patient Care is a listed category in which cost comparisons are not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Health care delivery and patient care activities are generally exempt from A-76 cost-comparisons; these should be identified and excluded early in study scoping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-comparison exemptions: Core capability
rubrics_metrics.description: Core Capability – generally related to technical capabilities – is a category where cost comparisons are not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an activity constitutes a core technical capability, it may be excluded from costing/comparison; define 'core capability' in context and document rationale when exempting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-comparison exemptions: Research and development
rubrics_metrics.description: Research and Development is listed as a category exempt from cost comparisons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: R&D activities are not routinely subject to A-76 cost comparisons; identify R&D elements in scope and exclude or specially handle them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-comparison exemptions: No satisfactory commercial source available
rubrics_metrics.description: If no satisfactory commercial source is available, a cost comparison is not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document market research showing lack of acceptable commercial providers before deciding not to perform cost comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-comparison exemptions: Small functions (10 or fewer FTE)
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions with 10 or fewer Full Time Employees (FTE) are exempt from cost comparison. For functions with 11 or more FTE a cost comparison is not needed if a fair and reasonable price can be obtained through competition and affected Federal employees are reassigned to comparable positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use staffing thresholds to screen tasks; for small functions consider streamlined handling and document reassignments/assurances when larger functions rely on streamlined procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-comparison exemptions: Government exceeds industry performance/cost standards
rubrics_metrics.description: If current government performance exceeds generally recognized industry performance and cost standards, cost comparisons are not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide objective evidence (benchmarks, metrics) that government performance and costs are superior before bypassing cost comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-comparison exemptions: Temporary authorizations for in-house performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Temporary authorizations for in-house performance are an exemption to performing cost comparisons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use temporary authorizations sparingly and document timeframe and rationale; do not use as a substitute for proper A-76 analysis when long-term sourcing is intended.

rubrics_metrics.name: A-76 cost-comparison process (six major steps)
rubrics_metrics.description: When cost comparison is required there are six major steps: (1) Development of a Performance Work Statement (PWS) and Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan (QASP); (2) Performance of a Management study to determine the Government's Most Efficient Organization (MEO); (3) Development of the in-house Government cost estimate; (4) Issue the Request for Proposal (RFP) or Invitation for Bid (IFB); (5) Comparison of the in-house bid against the proposed contract or Inter-service Support Agreement (ISSA) price; (6) Administrative appeal process to assure costs are fair, accurate and calculated per A-76.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow these ordered steps as the A-76 procedural core; each step has associated documentation and evidentiary standards (PWS/QASP, MEO assumptions, full costing) that must be defensible in protests and audits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance Work Statement (PWS) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The PWS "defines what is being requested, the performance standards and measures and timeframes of performance" and should be "performance-oriented, stating what outputs or measures are desired... yet does not indicate to the supplier how a service should be accomplished."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write PWS to avoid limiting service operations, arbitrarily increasing risk, reducing competition, violating industry norms, or omitting statutory/regulatory requirements. PWS clarity is critical to accurate cost estimates and avoiding post-award contract changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan (QASP) guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The QASP "describes the methods of inspections to be used, the reports required and the resources to be expended." It does not need to be published in the solicitation nor provided to government employees developing the management study; competitors are expected to develop their own QA plans based on the PWS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use QASP to define surveillance approach and evidence of performance; preserve QASP from over-prescribing methods while ensuring measurable metrics are available for contractor and MEO evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management Plan / Most Efficient Organization (MEO) development
rubrics_metrics.description: The Management Plan documents the Government's MEO and should "reflect the scope of the PWS and should identify the organizational structure needed... document the best structure, staffing, and operating procedures, equipment, and inspection plans... document the assumptions used in developing the MEO and in-house cost estimate, including assets of the organization, Quality-Assurance Plan, Transition Plan and the in-house cost estimate."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the MEO is realistic, fully documented, and uses defensible assumptions; capture transition costs, asset valuations, and staffing details to support the in-house cost estimate and withstand challenge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicitation and proposal handling per FAR and service regs
rubrics_metrics.description: Solicitations must be issued in accordance with the FAR, Service regulations and other statutory requirements; either IFB or RFP may be used depending on the nature of services. Proposals are treated the same as other competitions in terms of security of offers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select procurement vehicle (IFB/RFP) consistent with acquisition strategy and PWS. Follow standard procurement rules for responsiveness and responsibility; preserve confidentiality and fairness in opening/handling bids.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison, tentative decision and award procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: For sealed bids contracting officers open all bids including the in-house estimate and enter prices on the cost comparison form; a tentative decision is announced subject to evaluation for responsiveness and responsibility. For negotiated procurements, the most advantageous private sector or ISSA proposal is compared against the in-house estimate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain transparent and auditable records of the comparison and rationale for tentative decisions; ensure responsiveness/responsibility evaluations are applied consistently and documented to reduce protest risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative appeals and protest resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: The final step in the cost comparison process is resolution of any protests by unsuccessful offerors (private sector, ISSA or in-house). The administrative appeal process assures all costs on the Cost Comparison Form are fair, accurate and calculated in accordance with A-76.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate protests and ensure all cost inputs, assumptions, and procedures are defensible and well-documented; contracting officers have limited ability to mitigate protests—proper process and documentation reduce protest exposure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of full costing and Cost Comparison Form
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost comparisons must include full costing; the Cost Comparison Form is the tool used to compare in-house, contract, and ISSA prices and must contain fair and accurate cost entries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply A-76 costing rules (including labor, overhead, assets, transition costs) and document all calculations. GAO reviews have questioned DoD savings projections when costing and assumptions are weak—use conservative and auditable methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess projected savings critically and account for caveats
rubrics_metrics.description: Historical A-76 competitions showed savings (27% to 36%), but GAO and RAND cautioned that DoD/OMB lack reliable data, that mandated wage increases, poorly written PWS, and contractor low-balling can diminish realized savings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on headline savings estimates without sensitivity analysis; include contingencies, realistic wage assumptions, and robust PWS to avoid post-award cost growth or unrealized savings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and manage risks associated with competitive sourcing
rubrics_metrics.description: Risk identification and management within the A-76 process (including contract type, staffing, transition, PWS deficiencies, and contractor performance risks) must be examined and mitigated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use risk registers, appropriate contract types, performance metrics, transition plans, and oversight resources; learn from past lessons (litigation, protests, contractor low-balling, PWS deficiencies) to design mitigation measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify common family of services suitable for competition
rubrics_metrics.description: Research question: Is there a common family of installation support services across DoD being outsourced, and if so what services comprise that family? The thesis searches service-level data to identify nature and scope (e.g., facilities maintenance, base operations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use historical A-76 studies, surveys of contracting commands, and lessons learned to identify categories (and subservices like painting or plumbing) that are repeatedly competed and amenable to standard PWSs and acquisition strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staffing the competitive sourcing and source selection teams
rubrics_metrics.description: Chapters address "Staffing the competitive sourcing team" and "Staffing of source selection team" as essential management components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assemble multidisciplinary teams (contracting, technical, legal, QA, labor/HR) with clear roles for MEO development, cost estimation, PWS writing, and source selection to ensure credible studies and defensible outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop acquisition strategy and select contract type with risk considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: The acquisition strategy and contract type used in competitive sourcing affects the nature and amount of risk the installation must accept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how fixed-price, incentivized, award-fee, or other contract forms allocate performance and cost risk; choose contract type aligned with PWS clarity, market conditions, and risk mitigation objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition planning and documentation of assumptions/assets
rubrics_metrics.description: Management Plan must include Transition Plan and document assumptions used in in-house cost estimate, including assets of the organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly document transition timelines, costs (severance, training, equipment transfer), and asset valuations; include these in cost comparisons to avoid hidden costs and disputes post-award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate and learn from protests and litigation (lessons learned)
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey and literature review sections collect lessons learned and examine protests and litigation from past A-76 competitions to identify pitfalls for Contracting Officers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review GAO and Comptroller General decisions and service 'lessons learned' compilations; incorporate legal precedents and common protest grounds into study design, documentation practices, and procurement decisions.
